disclaimer: Fictional sample company. Generated data for demonstration, not measurements.

company.name: Cypress Harbor Credit Union
company.consumer_rules: CFPB rules (Regulation E, Regulation Z) apply; CFPB examines institutions over $10B in assets, so the credit union is examined by NCUA and the Florida Office of Financial Regulation.

assumptions.note: Request volumes, token sizes, cache hit rates and hours of use per app are illustrative assumptions (demo/cypress_harbor.py); budgets and per-key caps are the credit union's config/routes.yaml. Spend is tokens times list prices (on-prem Llama at an assumed GPU chargeback rate). Spend prevented by the anomaly pause is the runaway's rate until the next business morning, within the key, team and org caps (estimated, not measured).

incidents.handled: The circuit breaker on Claude Haiku 4.5 opened after 5 consecutive failures (failure_threshold: 5); later requests skipped it and went straight to GPT-4.1 mini, and half-open probes every 30 s closed it again at 2:17 pm. 109 requests were answered by the fallback; none failed.

notable.title: Twelve minutes of Anthropic overload, 109 requests answered by the fallback
notable.detail: Claude Haiku 4.5 returned 529 overloaded from 2:05 pm to 2:17 pm. After 5 consecutive failures its breaker opened, and smart-fast and fast-chat requests went straight to GPT-4.1 mini; no member-facing errors.

notable.title: Contractor key refused the heavy-reasoning route
notable.detail: A vendor developer's vendor-code-assist key (team contractors) asked for heavy-reasoning. The contractors policy allows only smart-fast, cheap-batch and local-first, so the gateway refused it with 403 before any provider saw the prompt; the developer resent it on local-first 24 seconds later.

notable.title: Looping coding agent paused 69 seconds after it started
notable.detail: From 2:06 pm an engineer's coding agent called heavy-reasoning in a fix-and-retest loop on the code-assistant key ($43.20 an hour). After 23 calls the key's spend that hour reached 10.2x its 7-day hourly baseline and the gateway paused it. Estimated spend prevented before 8 am the next business day: $12.72, the most the key daily cap ($7.50) allowed across the 2 UTC days the loop would have run.

notable.title: OpenAI incident absorbed by fallback
notable.detail: 47 minutes of 503 service unavailable on GPT-4.1 mini. fast-chat ranked the remaining deployments by latency and Claude Haiku 4.5 answered 62 requests; online and mobile banking chat kept answering, and the member assistant (smart-fast, Claude Haiku first) was not affected.

notable.title: August showback sent to department heads
notable.detail: CSV export by team, app and model: $872 in August against $1,099 in team budgets (79%). Risk analytics finished 55% under budget; member services came closest, at 84% of its budget.

notable.title: On-prem residency for regulated work moved into policy
notable.detail: regulated-fast already listed only the on-prem Llama deployment. config/policies.yaml now also sets allowed_providers: [ollama] and a required pii_redact hook for that route, so a later edit to routes.yaml cannot add a cloud fallback for dispute or BSA work.
